acip: [E111] BYANG SEMS 'PHAGS PA'I GZUGS MED PA'I SNYOMS PAR 'JUG PA'I RNAM PA BZHI CHOS CAN, THAR PA DANG MTHUN PAR GNAS PA'I LAM GYI RANG BZHIN YIN TE, RANG SA'I RO MYANG GI SGRIB PA LAS GROL PHYIR DU SGOM PA'I GZUGS MED KYI RNAM THAR YIN PA'I PHYIR,
wylie: [e111] byang sems 'phags pa'i gzugs med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa'i rnam pa bzhi chos can, thar pa dang mthun par gnas pa'i lam gyi rang bzhin yin te, rang sa'i ro myang gi sgrib pa las grol phyir du sgom pa'i gzugs med kyi rnam thar yin pa'i phyir
english: Let's consider (44–47) the four types of balanced meditation on the formless realm, as practiced by a bodhisattva who is also a realized being. These meditations have the basic nature of a path which is consistent with freedom; Because these are freedoms of the formless realm which we practice in order to free ourselves from the spiritual obstacle of becoming engrossed in the taste of the particular level we happen to be on.
